newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada spot gas slightly higher on storage demand.
newsitem.headline: Canada spot gas slightly higher on storage demand.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices were up slightly on Wednesday as buying of supply for storage injection remained strong in Alberta, traders said.
Also, a freak snowstorm in Alberta on Tuesday may have cut the ability of some gas plants to ship expected volumes.

Spot gas at the AECO storage hub was talked at C$1.61 per gigajoule in late trade, up about two cents from Tuesday, but down four cents from last week. June AECO fetched about C$1.65 per GJ, on par with last Wednesday's levels.
Storage injections at all four Alberta facilities were pegged at 1.17 billion cubic feet a day on Tuesday.
"Things are still stuck in the range, but up a bit," a Calgary-based trader said. "NOVA is drafting and field receipts may have been down because of the snow."

Alberta got an unexpected blast of winter weather on Tuesday with temperatures dropping to -2 Celsius (28 Fahrenheit). Twenty-eight cm (11 inches) of snow was dumped on Calgary, tripling a previous record set for May 20.
Environment Canada said Alberta temperatures were expected to remain unseasonably cold through Saturday, with overnight values dropping below freezing.

At Niagara in eastern Canada, prices were discussed in the US$2.36/2.38 range in quiet trade, down about a penny from Tuesday. June Niagara was quoted at NYMEX plus 19 cents, or about US$2.40 per mmBtu.
In the west, Sumas prices were talked in the US$1.28/1.29 range, unchanged from Tuesday. ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
